sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows:
• **Buddhism** founded by **Siddhartha Gautama** (The **Buddha** / 'The Enlightened One')
• Also known as **Shakyamuni** (Sage of the Shakya clan) and **Tathagata** ('One who has attained truth')

• Born in **563 BCE** at **Lumbini** (present-day Nepal near Kapilavastu)
• Clan: **Shakya** Kshatriya clan
• Father: **Suddhodana** (Ruler of Kapilavastu)
• Mother: **Mahamaya** (Koliya dynasty, died 7 days after birth)
• Foster Mother: **Gautami Prajapati** (First female monk in **Sangha**)

• Based on **Four Noble Truths** (Arya Satya) and **Eightfold Path** (Astangika Marga)
• Rejects authority of Vedas, ritual sacrifices, and caste hierarchy
• Believes in **Karma**, Rebirth, and **Nirvana** (Cessation of desire), while advocating the **Middle Path** (Madhyam Marg)

• **Great Renunciation (Mahabhinishkramana)**: Age **29**
• **Enlightenment (Nirvana)**: Age **35** at **Bodh Gaya** under a Pipal tree
• **First Sermon (Dharmachakra Pravartana)**: At **Sarnath**
• **Death (Mahaparinirvana)**: Age **80** (**483 BCE**) at **Kushinagar**

• Primary Scripture: **Tripitaka** (Three Baskets)
• Sacred Language of Early Texts: **Pali** (language of the common people)

• **Buddha** (The Enlightened One)
• **Dhamma** (The Teachings)
• **Sangha** (The Order of Monks & Nuns)

• High-yield history topic with 1-2 direct factual questions guaranteed every year
• Frequently asked areas: **Buddhist Councils**, **Life Symbols**, **Tripitaka** divisions, and **Sarnath/Bodh Gaya** facts

items.title: 1. Life Journey & Major Milestones of Gautam Buddha
items.content:
• **Early Life**: Named **Siddhartha**; married **Yashodhara** at age 16; had a son named **Rahul**.
• **Four Great Sights**: An **old man**, a **sick man**, a **dead body**, and an **ascetic** (inspired him to seek truth).
• **Teachers**: **Alara Kalama** (taught Sankhya philosophy at Vaishali) and **Uddaka Ramaputta** (at Rajgir).
• **Enlightenment**: Achieved on **Vaishakha Purnima** on the banks of **Niranjana River** (Falgu River) at **Bodh Gaya**.
• **First Sermon**: Delivered at **Deer Park (Rishipatana)** in **Sarnath** to 5 former companions (**Pancha Vaggiya**).
• **Mahaparinirvana**: Passed away at **Kushinagar** (Capital of Mallas) after consuming food served by **Cunda**.

items.title: 2. The Four Noble Truths (Arya Satya) & Triratna
items.content:
• **Dukkha**: Life is full of suffering (**Sabbam Dukkham**).
• **Dukkha Samudaya**: There is a cause for suffering (**Desire / Trishna / Taṇhā**).
• **Dukkha Nirodha**: Suffering can be ended by eliminating desire.
• **Dukkha Nirodha Gamini Pratipat**: The path leading to cessation of suffering is the **Eightfold Path**.
• **Mnemonic to remember Four Noble Truths**: **S-C-E-P** (**S**uffering → **C**ause → **E**nding → **P**ath).

items.title: 3. The Eightfold Path (Astangika Marga) - Divided into 3 Pillars
items.content:
• **Wisdom Pillar (Prajna)**:
  - **Right View (Samyak Drishti)**: Understanding the Four Noble Truths.
  - **Right Resolve (Samyak Sankalpa)**: Intention of renunciation and harmlessness.
• **Ethical Conduct Pillar (Sila)**:
  - **Right Speech (Samyak Vak)**: Abstaining from lies and harsh language.
  - **Right Action (Samyak Karmanta)**: Non-violence (Ahimsa) and ethical behavior.
  - **Right Livelihood (Samyak Ajiva)**: Earning living through honest means.
• **Mental Discipline Pillar (Samadhi)**:
  - **Right Effort (Samyak Vyayama)**: Preventing evil mental states.
  - **Right Mindfulness (Samyak Smriti)**: Awareness of body and mind.
  - **Right Concentration (Samyak Samadhi)**: Deep meditation and focus.
• **Mnemonic for 8-Fold Path Pillars**: **W-E-M** (**W**isdom, **E**thics, **M**editation).

items.title: 4. The Four Buddhist Councils (Sangeeti) Sequence
items.content:
• **1st Council (483 BCE)**: Location - **Rajgriha** (Sattaparni Cave) | Patron - **Ajatashatru** | President - **Mahakassapa** | Outcome - **Sutta Pitaka** and **Vinaya Pitaka** compiled.
• **2nd Council (383 BCE)**: Location - **Vaishali** | Patron - **Kalashoka** | President - **Sabakami** | Outcome - Split into **Sthaviravada** and **Mahasanghika**.
• **3rd Council (250 BCE)**: Location - **Pataliputra** | Patron - **Ashoka** | President - **Moggaliputta Tissa** | Outcome - **Abhidhamma Pitaka** compiled; decision to send missionaries.
• **4th Council (72 AD)**: Location - **Kundalvana (Kashmir)** | Patron - **Kanishka** | President - **Vasumitra** (Vice Pres: **Asvaghosa**) | Outcome - Formal split into **Hinayana** and **Mahayana**.
• **Mnemonic for Kings**: **A-K-A-K** (**A**jatashatru, **K**alashoka, **A**shoka, **K**anishka).
• **Mnemonic for Venues**: **R-V-P-K** (**R**ajgriha, **V**aishali, **P**ataliputra, **K**ashmir).

items.title: 5. Canonical Literature: The Tripitaka (Pali Canon)
items.content:
• **Sutta Pitaka**: Contains Buddha's discourses and sermons. Compiled by **Ananda**. Divided into 5 Nikayas (**Digha**, **Majjhima**, **Samyutta**, **Anguttara**, **Khuddaka**).
• **Vinaya Pitaka**: Contains rules and regulations for monastic discipline in **Sangha**. Compiled by **Upali**.
• **Abhidhamma Pitaka**: Contains philosophical and psychological interpretations of Dhamma. Compiled by **Moggaliputta Tissa** during 3rd Council.
• **Mnemonic for Tripitaka Focus**: **S-V-A** → **S**utta (**S**ermons), **V**inaya (**V**alues/Rules), **A**bhidhamma (**A**nalysis/Philosophy).

items.title: 6. Major Schools / Sects of Buddhism
items.content:
• **Hinayana (Lesser Vehicle / Theravada)**:
  - Believes in original teachings of Buddha as a **human teacher**.
  - Idol worship **forbidden**; uses symbols for worship.
  - Primary language: **Pali**.
  - Goal: **Arhat** (Individual salvation).
• **Mahayana (Greater Vehicle)**:
  - Treats Buddha as a **God** / Divine figure.
  - Promotes **Idol worship** and prayer.
  - Primary language: **Sanskrit**.
  - Goal: **Bodhisattva** (Salvation for all beings).
• **Vajrayana (Vehicle of Thunderbolt)**:
  - Developed around 6th-7th Century AD in Bengal & Bihar.
  - Involves **Tantric rituals**, mantras, and female deities (**Tara**).

sections.title: Comprehensive Data Tables
rows:
President: **Moggaliputta Tissa**
Outcome: **Abhidhamma Pitaka** compiled; Buddhist monks sent abroad

items.definition: Remember **A-K-A-K** for the patrons of 4 councils: **A**jatashatru (1st) → **K**alashoka (2nd) → **A**shoka (3rd) → **K**anishka (4th).

items.term: Trick 2: Council Venue Sequence (Ravana Visits Patna Kashmir)
items.definition: Remember **R-V-P-K**: **R**ajgriha → **V**aishali → **P**ataliputra → **K**ashmir.
Remember **M-S-M-V**: **M**ahakassapa (1st) → **S**abakami (2nd) → **M**oggaliputta Tissa (3rd) → **V**asumitra (4th).

items.term: Trick 4: Five Life Symbols Associated with Buddha
items.definition:
• **Birth**: Lotus & Bull
• **Great Renunciation**: Horse (Kanthaka)
• **Enlightenment**: Bodhi Tree (Pipal)
• **First Sermon**: Wheel (Dharmachakra)
• **Mahaparinirvana**: Stupa / Footprints

• 1st Council created **2 Pitakas** (**Sutta** & **Vinaya**).
• 3rd Council added the **3rd Pitaka** (**Abhidhamma**).
• Quick phrase: **S**ermons first (**Sutta**), **V**alues second (**Vinaya**), **A**nalysis last (**Abhidhamma**).

items.term: Trick 6: Mahayana vs Hinayana Language Trick
items.definition:
• **Hinayana** = **Pali** (Pali is older, Hinayana kept old texts).
• **Mahayana** = **Sanskrit** (Sanskrit gained popularity later under Kushans).

• **G**autami Prajapati (First female monk/Foster mother)
• **Y**ashodhara (Wife)
• **M**ahamaya (Biological Mother)
Buddha attained enlightenment at **Bodh Gaya** (under Bodhi Tree), but delivered his **first sermon** at **Sarnath** (Deer Park). UPSSSC frequently swaps these two venues.
**Kalashoka** hosted the **2nd** Council at Vaishali, while **Ashoka** hosted the **3rd** Council at Pataliputra. Do not mix their dynasty order (Shishunaga vs Maurya).

items.term: Misattributing the Compilation of Abhidhamma Pitaka
items.definition: Abhidhamma Pitaka was **NOT** compiled in the 1st Council. Only **Sutta** and **Vinaya** Pitakas were compiled in the 1st Council. Abhidhamma was added in the **3rd Council**.

items.term: Confusing Language of Hinayana and Mahayana Scriptures
items.definition: Hinayana literature is strictly in **Pali**, whereas Mahayana literature is predominantly in **Sanskrit** (e.g., works of Asvaghosa, Nagarjuna).

items.term: Mixing up First Sermon Name and Death Name
items.definition:
First Sermon = **Dharmachakra Pravartana** (Turning of the Wheel of Law).
Death = **Mahaparinirvana** (Final passing away).
**Anatta** (No-Self / Non-existence of permanent soul) belongs to **Buddhism**. **Anekantavada** (Theory of Pluralism/Many-sidedness) belongs to **Jainism**.
Buddhism is an **Heterodox (Nastika)** school of Indian philosophy; it explicitly **rejects Vedic authority**, ritual sacrifices, and caste superiority.
Gautam Buddha was born as **Siddhartha** in **563 BCE** at **Lumbini** in the **Shakya** Kshatriya clan.
At age **29**, Siddhartha left his home in search of truth on his horse **Kanthaka** and charioteer **Channa**.
Attained enlightenment at age **35** under a **Pipal Tree** at **Bodh Gaya** on the bank of **Niranjana River**.
Delivered first sermon at **Sarnath** (Deer Park) to 5 disciples; marked by the **Wheel** symbol.
Died in **483 BCE** at age **80** at **Kushinagar** under a Sal tree in the territory of **Mallas**.
1. Life is suffering, 2. Cause is desire, 3. Suffering can end, 4. Path is the **Eightfold Path**.
Divided into **Prajna** (Wisdom), **Sila** (Ethical Conduct), and **Samadhi** (Meditation).
The core pillars of Buddhism: **Buddha**, **Dhamma**, and **Sangha**.
Written in **Pali** language; consists of **Sutta Pitaka** (Discourses), **Vinaya Pitaka** (Rules), and **Abhidhamma Pitaka** (Philosophy).
Held at **Rajgriha** under patron **Ajatashatru** and president **Mahakassapa**; Sutta & Vinaya Pitakas compiled.
Held at **Vaishali** under patron **Kalashoka** and president **Sabakami**; first schism occurred.
Held at **Pataliputra** under patron **Ashoka** and president **Moggaliputta Tissa**; Abhidhamma Pitaka added.
Held at **Kundalvana (Kashmir)** under patron **Kanishka** and president **Vasumitra**; split into **Hinayana** and **Mahayana**.

• **Asvaghosa**: Wrote *Buddhacharita* and *Saundarananda* in Sanskrit.
• **Nagasena**: Author of *Milinda Panho* (Dialogue with Indo-Greek King Menander).

• **Nalanda**: Founded by **Kumaragupta I** (Gupta Dynasty).
• **Vikramashila**: Founded by **Dharmapala** (Pala Dynasty).

upscNotes.content: UPSSSC PET Frequently Asks: Match the following for Life Events vs. Symbols (Birth = Lotus/Bull, Renunciation = Horse, Enlightenment = Bodhi Tree, Sermon = Wheel, Death = Stupa). Memorize this exact mapping.
Don't confuse the venues of Buddhist Councils with Jain Councils. Buddhist Councils: Rajgriha, Vaishali, Pataliputra, Kashmir. Jain Councils: Pataliputra, Vallabhi.
Always remember the language connection: Pali is associated with early Buddhism and Hinayana, whereas Sanskrit gained prominence in Mahayana Buddhism under King Kanishka.
Beware of options listing 'Moggaliputta Tissa' as president of the 4th Council. He presided over the 3rd Council under Ashoka. Vasumitra presided over the 4th Council.

keyTakeaways: Gautam Buddha was born in 563 BCE in Lumbini and attained enlightenment under a Bodhi tree in Bodh Gaya at age 35.
The First Sermon was delivered at Sarnath (Dharmachakra Pravartana) and death occurred at Kushinagar (Mahaparinirvana) in 483 BCE.
Core tenets include the Four Noble Truths, Eightfold Path (Astangika Marga), and Triratna (Buddha, Dhamma, Sangha).
Canonical literature comprises the Tripitaka (Sutta, Vinaya, Abhidhamma Pitakas) composed in Pali language.
Four Buddhist Councils were hosted by Ajatashatru (Rajgriha), Kalashoka (Vaishali), Ashoka (Pataliputra), and Kanishka (Kashmir).
4th Council permanently split Buddhism into Hinayana (Theravada/Orthodox) and Mahayana (Idol worship/Sanskrit texts).
